info.name: LiteLLM Gateway on EKS (models, MCP, A2A)
info.description: Requests for the LiteLLM gateway built in this repository: health, model registration, inference, the MCP gateway, A2A agents, and virtual keys. Set `litellm_api_key` to the master key and keep `base_url` at the port-forward (http://127.0.0.1:4000). See docs/setup-guide.md.

Client-side function calling on `gemini-3-flash-preview`: the model answers with a `tool_calls` block for the declared `add()` function instead of text — your client is expected to execute it and reply.
Reasoning-model call (`deepseek-v4-pro-0813`). Note `max_completion_tokens` (not `max_tokens`) so the thinking budget isn't starved. Prompted with a Wheel of Time lore question.

Targets the `smart-router` alias — LiteLLM's routing strategy picks the underlying deployment per request. KNOWN ISSUE (2026-09-07): the proxy's `smart-router` (auto_router/complexity_router) currently resolves to `gpt-4o`, which has no deployment on this proxy, so LiteLLM answers 400 'no healthy deployments'. The 2xx assertion stays as the target; fix the router's target models in the LiteLLM UI (Models → smart-router).

item.description: One request per inference surface, each pinned to a proven model — swap `model` for anything in *List Available Models*. Covers plain chat (gpt-5.6-sol), client-side function calling (gpt-5.4-mini), a reasoning model (deepseek-v4-pro, `max_completion_tokens`), the smart-router alias, Voyage embeddings, DALL·E 3, Nano Banana Pro image generation through chat completions (OpenRouter), and Whisper transcription (re-pick the audio file in Body → form-data first).

item.name: 4 · MCP Gateway
Manage registrations (/v1/mcp/server)

request.description: All registered MCP servers. The test script prints name -> id -> url and stores the first id in {{mcp_server_id}}.
Runs the MCP handshake from the LiteLLM pod without storing anything. Expect {"status":"ok"}.
Registers a streamable-HTTP MCP server. `transport` must be set to `http` (the default is `sse`). `server_name` and `alias` must not contain a hyphen: LiteLLM names tools `<alias>-<tool>`.

body.raw:
{
  "server_name": "kagent_tools",
  "alias": "kagent_tools",
  "transport": "http",
  "url": "http://kagent-tools.kagent.svc.cluster.local:8084/mcp",
  "description": "kagent built-in tool server (kagent-tools 0.2.1). Read-only subset: the gateway hides every tool that changes the cluster.",
  "allowed_tools": [
    "k8s_get_resources",
    "k8s_describe_resource",
    "k8s_get_events",
    "k8s_get_pod_logs",
    "k8s_get_resource_yaml",
    "k8s_get_available_api_resources",
    "k8s_get_cluster_configuration",
    "helm_list_releases",
    "helm_get_release",
    "datetime_get_current_time"
  ]
}

request.description: MCP inside a chat completion: with require_approval 'never' the proxy lists the server's tools, executes the model's tool calls and makes one follow-up model call. Needs a registered model.

item.description: POST `/v1/chat/completions` with `tools: [{type: 'mcp', server_url: 'litellm_proxy', require_approval: 'never'}]` — the proxy exposes every registered MCP tool to the model and executes tool calls server-side, looping until the model answers. Scope with `x-mcp-servers` header if you want fewer servers in play.
Optional MCP examples. Deploy an MCPServer through kmcp, then register its internal service URL in LiteLLM before using these requests.

item.name: 5 · A2A Agents
Manage registrations (/v1/agents)

request.description: All registered agents. Optional query params: ?filter_reachable=true probes each agent's URL and drops unreachable ones; ?task=... ranks agents by semantic similarity over name/description/skills (needs agent_search_embedding_model configured).

Registers the kagent agent. The fields come from the card kagent serves at http://kagent-controller.kagent.svc.cluster.local:8083/api/a2a/kagent/cluster-agent/.well-known/agent-card.json. The url must be reachable from the LiteLLM pod.
Fetch one registered agent by id — returns the stored agent card and its metadata.
Unregisters from the gateway only — the kagent agent itself keeps running.

item.description: The beta agent registry. An agent is registered by submitting its A2A agent card; LiteLLM then proxies it at /a2a/{agent_id}. Our four kagent agents were registered by fetching each card from kagent-controller (/api/a2a/kagent/<name>/.well-known/agent-card.json) and submitting it verbatim as agent_card_params.

item.name: Invoke through the gateway (/a2a/{agent_id})

request.description: The same discovery contract as kagent serves, now via one gateway URL per agent.
One JSON-RPC call; behind it kagent runs the agent's tool loop, with the model and the tools both reached through this gateway. {{agent_id}} may be the agent id or its name (cluster_agent).

item.description:
LiteLLM proxies each registered agent's A2A surface. RESPONSE SHAPE: unlike calling kagent directly, the gateway nests the reply under result.task — state at result.task.status.state (TASK_STATE_COMPLETED) and the answer text at result.task.artifacts[].parts[].text. Agents run multi-round tool loops on GPT-5.6 Sol: allow 30-180s (raise Postman's request timeout).

AUTH: public via the key-only route (either header form). Port-forward: identical.
Optional A2A examples. Create a kagent Agent first, then register its reachable agent-card URL with LiteLLM.
